title: The App Powerhouse That Runs Like It's Day One
hook: How do you build a global app business on your own terms?
description: PicCollage CEO and co-founder John Fan breaks down the journey from an investor-backed startup to a profitable, self-sustaining powerhouse, all while preserving the startup culture along the way.
takeaways: Accidental PMF: catching viral traction by solving social media's early single-photo limitation.
Stepping off the VC treadmill: pivoting from external funding to a sustainable subscription model.
Culture by design: using rituals like "lightning demos" and global diversity to keep 100+ team members agile and creative.
AI with less "AI": offering new tech as "magic effects" to enhance user creativity without the hype.

title: Or Have Gen Z Founders Already Arrived?
hook: What drove Caleb Chu to become an entrepreneur at 16 and run a VC by 25?
description: Caleb Chu, founding partner of Nova Studio and venture partner at StarWorks, unpacks his journey from the early "battle scars" of his first startup to pioneering a hands-on venture studio model that builds side-by-side with Gen Z founders.
takeaways: Ditching conventional academic pressure for real-world exploration and entrepreneurship.
What it takes to discover and "trust" early-stage founders.
Empowering the next generation through platforms like the inaugural Boba Tech Summit and Stanford ASES Taiwan.
His long-term vision to reinvent higher education.

title: Building Physical AI: Inside MetAI's NVIDIA-Backed Tech
hook: How do you train your robot?
description: Daniel Yu, co-founder and CEO of NVIDIA-backed MetAI, dives into the next frontier of industrial innovation: physical AI. Robots and autonomous systems cannot learn from text alone.
takeaways: How MetAI uses digital twins and synthetic data as virtual training grounds for robotic arms, humanoids and "lights-out" factories.
How they are working with NVIDIA to bridge the AI adoption gap with 3D.
Why the startup has had to grow its team almost 10x in one year.
What founders in Taiwan can learn from founders in the US about storytelling and specialization.

title: Mark Birch: Tapping Into Community Value, Taiwan's AI Power
hook: Is the "lone founder" myth holding startups back?
description: TribeROI founder and CEO Mark Birch breaks down how community helps founders and why it is the ultimate force multiplier for high-growth companies. Also author of Community-in-a-Box, he launched the company to help businesses see their community data better and discover the value within.
takeaways: Why he left New York City to build his software startup in Taiwan. It wasn't just the Taiwan Employment Gold Card.
How agentic AI can turn community engagement into measurable business outcomes, from sales growth to innovation.
The opportunity to develop a world-class software startup ecosystem outside of Silicon Valley, despite what some say.

title: Camila Sáenz: Unlocking the Global Mindset With TUTEEMI
hook: What does it take to build a thriving business far from home?
description: Camila Sáenz shares her journey from foreigner to founder. She built TUTEEMI into one of Taiwan's most inspiring education startups, scaling with global accelerator AppWorks. Rather than rigid test prep, she wanted to give students confidence, curiosity, and a true global mindset.
takeaways: Vision conviction: when Covid-19 pushed education online, she doubled down on authentic, in-person mentorship.
Founder in a foreign land: how she turned cultural gaps into her business edge.
Weighing investor counsel: why investors are not always right.
Exporting the Taiwan experience: what Guatemala and other Latin American ecosystems can learn from Taiwan.

title: Jac Hsieh: Building NunoX and His Generational Dream
hook: From pivoting his first startup to pioneering textile AI.
description: In the debut episode of Startup DNA, the founder of NunoX reveals his journey of modernizing his family's tailoring legacy, eliminating fashion waste through digitization, and building a people-centric startup culture.
takeaways: Evolving NunoX: how Jac bridged the gap between textile manufacturers and global brands.
Redefining fundraising: why cultivating investor relationships matters more than sculpting the perfect pitch.
Founder's mindset: how to turn self-doubt into a superpower and why overthinking kills progress.
The ultimate goal: shifting the focus from material wealth to massive environmental impact.

title: From Anonymous to Autonomous: STR8 Sets Sail on Edge AI at Sea
hook: What happens when a retired U.S. Naval Officer meets a veteran hardware venture builder? Startup at first sight.
description: STR8 Industries, a deep tech maritime autonomy company, emerges from stealth at InnoVEX/Computex. The US-Taiwan startup is building high-performance "drone boats" that tap Taiwan's elite tech, computing, and shipbuilding ecosystem while delivering a plug-and-play platform for maritime security, data collection, and remote inspection.
takeaways: The synergy: the chance meeting over drinks (thankfully not at 2 A.M.) that led to a cutting-edge business.
The autonomy framework: a 3-point model of consequence, reversibility, and connectivity that redefines autonomy and control.
Ship fast, iterate faster: a relentless obsession with user feedback to solve real-world maritime demands.

title: Solving AI's Biggest Enterprise Flaws: Inside Synvo AI
hook: Artificial intelligence is the greatest recent breakthrough for humankind. But what is it still missing? The gem is in the context.
description: Saim ("Sam") Yeong Harng, co-founder and CEO of Synvo AI, a spinout from Nanyang Technological University's AI lab, on building the definitive enterprise memory layer for agentic systems.
takeaways: The core fix: how "contextual engineering" compresses fragmented, multimodal data to eliminate AI hallucinations and bypass tight context windows.
On-device privacy: why data security means moving away from public cloud models.
Strategic Taiwan: targeting mid-sized manufacturing firms and large corporates, with Taiwan as a strategic gateway.

title: Vellex Computing: Faster, Cheaper, Off-Cloud With Analog Intelligence
hook: An AI that trains itself and is accessible to many?
description: Dr. Palak Jain, co-founder and CEO of Stanford spinout Vellex Computing, on making AI training faster, cheaper, and more accessible. Vellex is a winner of the IC Taiwan Grand Challenge and the Plug and Play Taiwan Pitch Contest.
takeaways: Democratizing AI: moving training off the cloud to unlock the potential of everyday devices.
Analog intelligence: why returning to analog computing is essential for sustainable AI growth.
On-device adaptation: enabling robots and smart devices to learn and improve on the job.
Global journey: the story behind Vellex's roots in India, Singapore, and Stanford.

title: Visual AI: How Oculi Wants Machines to See
hook: Cameras are just digital mirrors. What would true machine vision look like?
description: Dr. Charbel Rizk, founder and CTO of Oculi, on redefining how devices "see" the world with a smart, programmable vision sensor that mimics the human eye.
takeaways: Vision vs. imaging: why cameras are just digital mirrors and how Oculi's technology mimics the human eye for true visual intelligence.
The Oculi chip: a smart, programmable CMOS vision sensor that processes relevant data efficiently, saving energy and money.
Real-world applications: from smart home automation to privacy-protecting motion sensors that distinguish between people and pets.
Global expansion: why Oculi is seeking partners in Taiwan's semiconductor ecosystem.

title: Amity Robotics: Humanizing AI Robots
hook: More and more we'll find ourselves talking to robots at hotels, airports and shopping malls, even hospitals.
description: Lionel Chin, COO of Amity Robotics, on driving startup growth as an "intrapreneur": deploying to 9 countries and securing global clients like IHG hotels and Southeast Asia's biggest malls in just 16 months.
takeaways: AI-powered customer experience: creating an interactive experience with non-humanoid autonomous concierge robots.
The accent problem: building custom speech models to humanize the AI voice and understand diverse global dialects, accents and tones.
Eye on Taiwan: how advanced manufacturing, robust tourism and a skilled labor pool make it their next pilot market.

title: Lean Mobility: Fast Track to Global Roads?
hook: What happens when you combine Japanese automotive engineering with Taiwan's manufacturing muscle?
description: Lean Mobility's lead investor and board member Ryan Yang reveals how this cross-border venture, founded by former Toyota Chief Engineer Akihiro Yanaka, is revving up to disrupt the global mobility landscape.
takeaways: The Toyota DNA: how founder Akihiro Yanaka persisted with the vision behind Toyota's i-Road project.
The synergy: Japanese tech expertise meets Taiwanese angel investment and manufacturing.
Global strategy: leaning on Japan's "kei car" market traits and eyeing Europe's mature micromobility landscape from day one.
The roadmap: a simultaneous launch in Japan and Taiwan.
